q-304130.solution:
This time, we'll use $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ notation. First, we compute the derivative, which gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(__a__x-__b__\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(__a__x-__b__{x}^{1/2}) \\  & =__a__-__b__\cdot \frac{1}{2}{x}^{-1/2} \\  & =__a__-\frac{__half_b__}{\sqrt{x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=__t__$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=__t__} & =__a__-\frac{__half_b__}{\sqrt{__t__}} \\  & =__term1__-__term2__ \\  & =__m__.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at the point $(__t__,__y__)$ is

$$
m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=__t__}=__m__.
$$

m={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=__t__}=__m__.
